prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1100; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured states the other vehicle crossed the center line during a turn. No airbags deployed. Both vehicles driven from scene. Photos requested from insured and assigned to field appraiser.

Entry 2: Insured reports mild neck pain the following morning and has visited an urgent care clinic for evaluation. Diagnosis noted as cervical strain. Claimant has retained counsel, who has requested that all communication be routed through the firm. Letter of representation received and logged. Future contact with claimant suspended pending counsel's direction.

Entry 3: Field appraisal completed on insured vehicle. Front bumper cover cracked, hood latch misaligned, and minor damage to the radiator support noted. Estimate prepared and submitted to repair shop for supplement review. Photos uploaded to claim file. Liability on the other vehicle remains under review pending police report.

Entry 4: Medical records requested through counsel's office for the cervical strain treatment. Counsel's office indicates a demand package will follow once treatment concludes. Physical therapy referral noted in the medical summary received so far. No surgical recommendation at this time. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury evaluation and continuing treatment.

Entry 5: Police report obtained and reviewed. Officer's narrative supports the account that the opposing vehicle crossed into the insured's lane. Liability assessment moved to probable adverse party. Subrogation notice prepared for the other carrier. File flagged for follow-up on medical status and receipt of demand package from counsel.
